markets: Homeowners and utility programmes in California and other US states; no international activity.
rationale: US residential energy firm with limited scale and no international footprint; weak F1 fit.

name: ACME Group
desc: Indian renewable energy group developing solar, wind and storage plants and green hydrogen and ammonia projects.
markets: Power plants across Indian states; overseas green ammonia project in Oman reported as planned.
rationale: B2B power developer with a growing profile in India; F1 could support its green fuels story.

name: Bord na Mona
desc: Irish state-owned company moving from peat harvesting to wind, biomass, solar and recycling businesses.
markets: Operations in Ireland with recycling and energy activity in the United Kingdom.
rationale: State-owned firm with a domestic focus and little marketing budget; weak F1 fit.

name: Hera
desc: Italian multi-utility group supplying gas, electricity, water, district heating and waste management services, with municipalities as main shareholders.
markets: Customers mainly in northern and central Italy; no major international operations.
rationale: Italian utility with consumer brand and local public shareholders; Imola GP is nearby but fit is modest.

name: HIF Global
desc: Develops facilities producing e-fuels such as e-methanol and e-gasoline from green hydrogen and captured carbon.
markets: Projects in Chile, the United States, Uruguay and Australia, backed by industrial investors.
rationale: E-fuels match F1's sustainable fuel push and offer technology showcase; still pre-commercial with limited marketing scale.

name: Kuntian New Energy
desc: Produces anode materials for lithium-ion batteries sold to battery cell makers in China.
markets: Customers presumed to be Chinese battery makers; no verified overseas sales.
rationale: B2B materials supplier with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit despite the electrification theme.

name: Leeward Renewable Energy
desc: Owns and operates wind, solar and storage projects across the United States, selling power under long-term contracts.
markets: Projects in many US states; no international operations.
rationale: US-only B2B power producer without consumer brand; Austin and Miami races give local reach but fit is weak.

name: Patterson-UTI Energy
desc: Provides contract drilling, hydraulic fracturing and related well services to oil and gas producers in North America.
markets: Drilling and completion services in the United States and Canada, with minor Middle East activity.
rationale: Oilfield services firm with B2B customers only; limited marketing need and weak F1 fit.

name: PowerCo
desc: Volkswagen Group's battery company developing and producing unified battery cells and gigafactories in Europe and North America.
markets: Gigafactories at Salzgitter, Valencia and St. Thomas in Ontario, supplying Volkswagen Group brands.
rationale: Part of Volkswagen Group, whose Audi brand joins F1 in 2026; battery technology gives a natural showcase.
f1: Part of Volkswagen Group, owner of Audi, which enters F1 in 2026 as a works team

name: Broad Reach Power
desc: Independent power producer that develops, owns and operates battery storage projects selling grid services in the United States.
markets: Storage projects in Texas and California; no international operations.
rationale: B2B storage developer with no consumer brand and a US-only footprint, so F1 fit is weak.

name: Clean Energy Fuels
desc: Supplies renewable natural gas and compressed natural gas to fleets through fuelling stations in the United States and Canada.
markets: Fuelling stations serving trucks, buses and refuse fleets in the United States and Canada.
rationale: Fleet fuel supplier; F1 sustainable fuels theme loosely fits but customers are B2B fleets and US-only.

name: Enel Green Power Hellas
desc: Greek renewable energy subsidiary of Enel Green Power operating wind, solar and hydro plants and selling power into Greece's grid.
markets: Wind, solar and hydro assets in Greece selling to the Greek grid.
rationale: Local subsidiary of Enel with no separate marketing budget; weak F1 fit.

name: ENN Energy Research Institute
desc: Research arm of the ENN Group developing clean energy technologies such as hydrogen, solar and fusion.
markets: Research based in China within ENN Group; overseas activity not confirmed.
rationale: Corporate research unit with no consumer brand or marketing need; very weak F1 fit.

name: Enviva
desc: Produces industrial wood pellets in the southeastern United States and ships them to power generators in Europe and Asia.
markets: Pellet plants in the US Southeast exporting to utilities in Europe, the United Kingdom, Japan and South Korea.
rationale: B2B biomass supplier with a controversial sustainability profile and little marketing culture; weak F1 fit.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 in 2024 and emerged as a private company in late 2024

name: SolarEdge Technologies
desc: Makes solar inverters, power optimisers, batteries and monitoring software for residential, commercial and utility solar systems worldwide.
markets: Sells through distributors and installers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Global energy-technology brand selling to installers; F1 offers technology showcase and B2B hospitality, though budgets are stretched.

name: Ara Partners
desc: Private equity firm investing in industrial decarbonisation and energy transition businesses in North America and Europe.
markets: Invests in industrial and energy transition companies in North America and Europe.
rationale: Private equity firm with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality could suit investor relations but fit is weak.

name: BEWi
desc: Produces expanded polystyrene packaging, insulation and other plastic and recycling products for customers across Northern Europe.
markets: Production and sales across the Nordics, the Baltics and other European countries.
rationale: B2B materials maker with industrial customers; limited consumer branding and weak F1 fit.
